decisions.reason: Audio and web conferencing is a low-cost add-on to the voice portfolio whose prospects are still uncertain, so keeping the option open is cheap, though commoditisation makes abandonment plausible.
Early adoption by data centres and a financial hub shows the metro data-centre network is realizing its value and fits the firm's owned-infrastructure strategy, which justifies further commitment.
Optical spectrum connectivity has its own page, builds on owned fibre and matches the high-bandwidth direction, so its value is still unfolding at low incremental cost.
A number ordering portal is a cheap software option that supports the real-time provisioning strategy, so there is little reason to abandon it yet.
Carrier pre-selection telephony is a declining legacy service with limited upside, but it is cheap to maintain and the results so far do not yet clearly show its value cannot be realized.
Direct voice network connection fits enterprise and service-provider voice needs on existing infrastructure, so keeping the option costs little while demand resolves.
